description:
Close dense factorization and solve gaps after GEMM parity work lands.

## Background

PLE, echelon, invert, solve, determinant, and rank-deficient regimes must inherit the optimized GEMM/TRSM paths rather than remaining separate bottlenecks.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] PLE/echelon/invert/solve target rows are within 1.5x of the best accepted reference or faster, scoped per-cell by the maturity markers recorded in the 7e41400f evidence doc.
- [hard] Rank-deficient regimes are measured and optimized separately from full-rank regimes.
- [hard] A final dense linear-algebra report records raw numbers, ratios, and block-size/dispatch policy.

## Amendment - 2026-05-07 (user-approved, Path A propagation from 7e41400f)

Per AskUserQuestion 2026-05-07 (7e41400f closure), criterion #1 inherits the per-cell maturity-marker scoping established in `7e41400f`. Empirical basis: `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-7e41400f-invert-solve-det.md` and `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-4eb105f7-dense-la-parity-evidence.md`.

The 2 invert/uniform cells (n=256 + n=1024) are [aspirational] with documented algorithm-choice cause (Dumas-Pernet driver vs fflas in-place LU-reuse); follow-up tracked in `d1a5fea8` (Replace Dumas-Pernet inv() driver with in-place LU-reuse), filed as a sibling under this story.

All other dense LA cells (PLE, echelon, TRSM, solve, det, invert/deficient, invert/uniform/n=64) PASS [hard] per 4eb105f7 § 1.

Re-escalation threshold: re-escalate when `d1a5fea8` closes (revisit invert/uniform cells with fresh measurements).
